recipe_generation.prompt:
You are proposing compression recipes for a factored 1-bit weight-delta format. A recipe assigns one integer rank to each layer TYPE; that rank is used for that layer type in all 24 transformer blocks (the embedding is a single matrix). The stored size of one matrix at rank r is priced exactly as:

  bytes(matrix, r) = ceil(rows * r / 8) + 4 * rows + 2 * cols * r

Layers (rows x cols of the delta matrix):
  embed: delta matrix 151936 x 896, rank may be 0..896
  attn.q_proj: delta matrix 896 x 896, rank may be 0..896
  attn.k_proj: delta matrix 128 x 896, rank may be 0..128
  attn.v_proj: delta matrix 128 x 896, rank may be 0..128
  attn.o_proj: delta matrix 896 x 896, rank may be 0..896
  mlp.gate: delta matrix 4864 x 896, rank may be 0..896
  mlp.up: delta matrix 4864 x 896, rank may be 0..896
  mlp.down: delta matrix 896 x 4864, rank may be 0..896

The total size of a recipe is bytes(embed) + 24 * (sum of bytes over the other 7 layer types), and it must be <= 19434496 bytes. That is exactly the cost of the uniform rank-32 recipe on this model; you have the same bytes, spend them differently.

The model pair is Qwen2.5-0.5B base and NuExtract-1.5-tiny, a fine-tune for structured JSON extraction (read a text and a JSON template, answer with the filled template). The finding you are designing against: this skill is gated by the FIRST generated token. The fine-tune starts the JSON; the plain base emits end-of-text immediately and answers nothing (0 of 10 test prompts). Our uniform rank-32 patch flips that gate on only 1 of 10 prompts (on the 9 others the patched model still stops immediately), even though the one extraction it does start is fully correct. Bigger uniform patches barely help (rank 64 and rank 128 each flip 2 of 10). So placement, not size, is the open question. Weigh protecting the embedding (it feeds every token position and, with tied weights, the output head) and the output-side layers (attn.o_proj, mlp.down) that shape the final logits, if you judge that is where the start-vs-stop decision lives.

Propose exactly 5 recipes, ordered best-first: put the recipe you recommend most first. Make them genuinely different from each other and from uniform: uneven allocations are the point. Every recipe must include every layer name exactly once in its "ranks" object, with an integer rank (0 is allowed and means that layer type's delta is dropped).

Reply with ONLY a JSON object, no markdown fences, no commentary, in exactly this shape:
{"recipes": [{"name": "<short name>", "reason": "<one sentence>", "ranks": {"embed": 0, "attn.q_proj": 0, "attn.k_proj": 0, "attn.v_proj": 0, "attn.o_proj": 0, "mlp.gate": 0, "mlp.up": 0, "mlp.down": 0}}]}
Replace the zeros with your ranks. Check your arithmetic: each recipe's total (embed once + 24 blocks) must be <= 19434496 bytes.

first_token_margins.definition: margin = logprob(fine-tune's actual first generated token) - logprob(end-of-text 151643) at the first generation position, natural log; positive means the gate is open (starting the JSON beats stopping)

conclusion: Placement did not beat size at equal bytes; it did worse. The Spark recipe's radical reallocation (embed 382, mlp.gate/up dropped to 0) opened 0 of 10 gates and its mean first-token margin (-4.14) is far below uniform rank 32 (-1.29). The gate-open counts measured from margins (base 0, rank32 1, recipe 0, full delta 10) exactly match the generation outcomes. Neither bigger uniform patches (2/10 at rank 128) nor this reallocation opens the gate at these budgets; uniform rank 32 is closest per byte.
